Hi Andre,

Good conversation today, thanks for walking me through the vision.

I've prepared questions for Angeli ahead of our session. Sharing them now so she can look through them in advance:

Grounding and governors

How is source-grounding enforced today?
Are the governors implemented as code, or as prompt instructions? Where do they live in the repo?
What happens when the model has insufficient context: is there a defined state that blocks generation and triggers clarifying questions?
Is there a stored representation of what the agent knows about a business, or is context rebuilt from chat history each time?

Data and Supabase

How is multi-tenancy handled: RLS policies or application-level filtering?

Codebase
Which parts would you rewrite given time, and which are stable?
Is the project TypeScript throughout, with strict mode on?

Process

How would you split work so we don't collide?
Biggest blocker to calling this production-ready?

Looking forward to tomorrow.

Hi Andre, two things I need from Anjali before I start:

A list of which routes and screens are actually built and worth reviewing at this stage. Reviewing scaffolded or unbuilt sections won't produce anything useful for a Release 1 recommendation.

Repo read access and a deployment URL if there is one.

Then, I'll come back with scope and a fixed price for the review.

Hi Svitlana, that makes sense. I will provide the list of R1 routes and screens that are sufficiently built for review.
Once the Upwork contract and confidentiality/IP arrangements are in place, we’ll provide named, read-only repo access and a staging URL. Production credentials and customer data will not be included.
Before access, please confirm the proposed review output will include:
a Release 1 readiness recommendation
prioritised findings and blockers, with supporting evidence
security, architecture, performance and maintainability risks
recommended remediation and indicative effort
clear assumptions and items excluded from the review
Please also provide an indicative price range or capped discovery allowance now. After reviewing the materials, you can confirm the final scope, fixed price and delivery date.

Confirmed: the review output will include all five items as you listed them:

Release 1 readiness recommendation
Prioritised findings and blockers with supporting evidence
Security, architecture, performance and maintainability risks
Recommended remediation with indicative effort per item
Stated assumptions and explicit exclusions

Two additions from my side. Each finding will reference the specific file and line so Anjali can act on it directly rather than re-investigating. And the deliverable will be a written document - no call required to interpret it, though I'm available if you want to walk through it.

Indicative pricing: $70/hr, with the review estimated at 8–12 hours, so $560–840. Whether you prefer to run it hourly or as a fixed price is your call; either works for me.

Contract and confidentiality terms are fine. Read-only access without production credentials or customer data is the right arrangement for this work.

Turnaround: three working days from access.

Hi Andre, three scope questions from the front-end review. All three are decisions rather than defects, so they're yours rather than Anjali's.

1\. Is the multi-user scenario in Release 1? The invite send exists, but the front end never calls POST /account/users/accept and there's no route for the invite link, so an invited user has nowhere to land. Making it work end-to-end also needs member-list, revoke and remove on the backend: none of those endpoints exist today.

2\. "Instant access revocation" is in the product description, but with #1427 open the disconnect endpoints return success without removing the connection record. The front end handles this correctly and refuses to claim success, so the claim and the behaviour don't currently match.

3\. Anjali's per-member metering requirements (token consumption per member, usage breakdown, individual limits) are implemented only in the superadmin console under /admin. The account owner has no access to any of them. Was an owner-facing view planned for R1, or is that Phase 2?
